finish.summary: I built a two-storey workbench organizer, 34 parts in all. The bottom storey is two half bases side by side, each with a drawer in its cut face. The top storey is two more half bases, each holding a half-depth bin split into two compartments. Every open edge has a solid end cap, and the joints are bolted. check_build reports no issues and the mesh check is clear. You asked for a drawer below and there are two: I added the second so the other half base's cut face wasn't left open. For staging, the bins hold a screwdriver and small heaps of M3 screws and nuts. These props aren't parts and aren't in the parts list. The screw and nut heaps are flagged as sitting below the bin rims, so they're hard to see from the side but show from above.

M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
